title: Chinese steel imports remain a threat to Indian industry: Tata Steel CEO
dek: Tata Steel's T V Narendran says Chinese imports remain a threat as domestic steelmakers continue talks with the government on protective measures.
summary: Tata Steel chief executive T V Narendran has said Chinese steel imports remain a threat to the Indian industry, according to The Hindu BusinessLine. He said domestic steelmakers are continuing discussions with the government on measures to protect the industry from cheap imports, while Indian producers invest in expanding capacity. The excerpt does not specify which measures are under discussion.
keyFacts: Tata Steel CEO T V Narendran describes Chinese imports as a continuing threat
Domestic steelmakers are in ongoing discussions with the government on protection from cheap imports
Indian producers are investing in capacity expansion
whyItMatters: Import pressure while large capacity additions come on stream could weigh on domestic realisations and utilisation rates. Industry lobbying suggests trade defence remains a live policy question.
implications: Producers will watch for any extension or tightening of trade remedies; buyers relying on imported material should factor in the possibility of further protective measures.
